# Lint gate census

**Generated by `scripts/census-lint-gates.mjs`. Do not hand-edit the first two columns.**
The **Also held by**, **Verdict** and **Evidence** columns are written by hand and are
preserved across regeneration — whether an invariant is independently held is a
judgement about the whole tree, and no script can make it.

**Method** (FR-R3-121 / FR-025): every `*.test.ts` under `repo/tests/lint/`,
**recursively**, one row each. The invariant line is the gate's own top-level
`describe` title, which is what its author already wrote to describe the rule. A flat
glob would miss `gate-integrity/` and produce a census that looks complete and is not.

**Retirement rule** (FR-021): a gate may be retired only when **Also held by** names a
specific control — a type that makes the violation unrepresentable, a generated contract
that would fail to regenerate, a compiler flag under the strictness ratchet, or a named
sibling gate refusing the same shape. *Seems covered*, *unlikely now* and *the code
moved* are not successors. **Zero retirements is a valid outcome**, and `FR-R3-121` §5
predicted it: its author sampled the set and found every gate well motivated.

| Figure | Value | Date | Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gate files | **201** | 2026-10-01 | `*.test.ts` under `tests/lint/` recursively |
| Marked `unique` | 179 | 2026-10-01 | hand verdict |
| Marked `partially redundant` | 22 | 2026-10-01 | hand verdict |
| Marked `redundant` | 0 | 2026-10-01 | hand verdict |

<!-- census:prose -->
The three verdict rows sum to the gate-file count, so they are one measurement and carry one
date. `FR-R3-163` moved the total 191 → 192 and `partially redundant` 15 → 16 on 2026-09-05;
the first draft of that edit bumped only the rows whose values changed, leaving **192** dated
2026-09-04 — a day on which there were 191. Mixed dates across figures a sum constrains is
itself the defect, because it claims they were counted at moments when they could not all
have held.

Placement note (2026-09-05): the paragraph above sat between the figure table and the marker
until feature 203 regenerated the census, which deleted it — everything above the marker is
rebuilt from the template on every run. Hand-written prose belongs here, below the marker.
















## Method, and what it does and does not establish

**Assigned 2026-08-27 (`FR-R3-121` / FR-020).** `FR-R3-121` §5 records that its author *"sampled
rather than read all 141"*, so this section is explicit about how far the verdicts below reach.

**Observed.** Every gate file was enumerated and its `describe` title read. Four mechanical
redundancy signals were computed across the whole set: gates whose subject is a **generated
contract**; gates naming a **compiler flag** under the strictness ratchet; **near-duplicate
implementations** sharing a scan helper and differing only by a constant and an allowlist; and
**name-cluster overlap**.

**What that found.** One cluster, evidenced rather than suspected: **twelve** of the thirteen
`no-inline-*` gates are one rule implemented twelve times, across **794 lines**. Diffing two of
them leaves the command constant, the allowlist and the prose; several say in their own headers
that they *"mirror the established pattern at"* a named sibling. And
`no-inline-backend-ping-ipc.test.ts` does the same job in **15 lines**, which is what makes this
evidence rather than an impression.

> **Corrected 2026-08-27**, while acting on this census's own recommendation. The original entry
> said **thirteen**. `no-inline-queue-item-template.test.ts` is **not** in the family: it pins the
> single render path of a Svelte row template and shares only the filename prefix. The first pass
> generalised from diffing two files and a name; checking all thirteen found the exception.
>
> Left visible rather than edited away, because it is exactly the limit this section states — and
> because a consolidation that had trusted "thirteen" would have folded a Svelte template gate into
> an IPC allowlist table.

> **Re-measured 2026-09-14** (`FR-R3-174`, T1754). The total above read **roughly 930 lines** until
> now, and the correction directly above it is what made that wrong. Dropping
> `no-inline-queue-item-template.test.ts` from the family removed a **77-line** member from the very
> set the total sums. The membership was corrected; the number that membership determines was left
> alone, one clause away, for eighteen days.
>
> That is the failure this re-measurement exists to exhibit, and it is why **794** is now derived
> rather than transcribed: `tests/lint/asserted-counts.test.ts` registers this claim against the
> twelve files themselves, and its entry also pins the family at twelve, so neither a resized member
> nor a thirteenth one can pass silently again. The exemplar's **15 lines** beside it is deliberately
> *not* registered — see the decision in
> `docs/operations/asserted-counts-sweep.md` for which figures earned an entry and which did not.

**Relied on.** That a gate's `describe` title describes its rule.

**Inferred, and this is the limit.** A `unique` verdict means *no sibling gate, type, generated
contract or compiler flag was found asserting the same invariant by the four signals above*. It
does **not** mean a human read all 151 gates against each other and proved independence. The
correction above is what that limit looks like when it bites.

## Retirements: none

**Zero, and that is the finding rather than an empty section.**

FR-021 permits a retirement only when a specific control now holds the invariant. No gate met that
bar. The one cluster with real redundancy is redundant in *machinery*, not in *rule* — retiring any
of the twelve would delete a command's single-call-site guarantee that nothing else holds.

**The recommendation the census produces instead** is consolidation: the twelve could become one
table-driven gate with twelve rows, on the shape `no-inline-backend-ping-ipc.test.ts` already
demonstrates, saving roughly 900 lines while keeping every rule.
`no-inline-queue-item-template.test.ts` stays as it is.

**Not taken, and the reason changed on inspection — 2026-08-27.**

The consolidation was attempted, specifically to test whether the risk that blocked it — an
allowlist transcribed wrong, silently widening what may call a mutating IPC command — could be
removed mechanically. **It can.** The allowlists are separable from the duplicated scan helper, so
the helper could be consolidated with no allowlist moving at all.

**The attempt found a better reason not to.** The twelve do not share one implementation. Their
`listMatchingFiles` helpers carry **three different failure semantics**, invisible until the bodies
are normalised and compared:

| Behaviour when the tree is partly unreadable (`status 2`) | Gates | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **A** — return `[]` | `catalog-history`, `read-metrics` | discards matches the scan *did* find |
| **B** — unhandled, so it throws | `phase-breakpoint`, `phase-control`, `phase-log`, `reorder`, `save-catalog`, `save-general-settings` | fails closed, loudly |
| **C** — return the matches found | `run-launcher`, `workflow-run` | most complete, and the only variant that explains itself: *"grep still writes the matches it did find to stdout, and the positive control below fails loudly if the scan came back empty"* |

Two more — `backend-ping` and `process-yaml` — have already migrated to the shared
`filesReferencing` and carry no local helper; `backend-ping` does the whole job in **15 lines**.

**So consolidation is not a tidying. It is choosing one failure semantics for twelve gates** — a
behavioural decision about how an IPC-authority gate behaves when the tree cannot be fully read.
`C` is the best-reasoned and is what to converge on, but adopting it changes what eight gates do
under that condition. That is a change to make deliberately and verify, not to fold into a
line-count reduction.

**Nothing is currently unsafe.** All eight `A`/`B` gates carry a positive `toContain` vacuity
control, so an empty or truncated scan fails the gate rather than passing it — verified for all
eight. The divergence is a maintainability defect, not a live hole.

**Then acted on, once the divergence was understood — 2026-08-27.**

Reading further killed the premise a second time. `filesMatching` **does not shell out**; neither
does `scanWebviewSources`. Both are `node:fs` walks, and `filesMatching` catches its own read errors
internally. So `err.status` is *always* `undefined`, every variant's conditions are always false, and
**every variant falls through to the same `throw err`.**

The three "failure semantics" were three flavours of **unreachable code** — `grep`/`rg` exit-code
handling left behind when the scan stopped being a subprocess. There was never a behavioural
difference to preserve.

It mattered anyway: reading those branches is what made a reviewer conclude the gates diverged and
defer this twice. **Dead error handling for a mechanism that is gone does not merely take up room —
it answers questions wrongly.**

**What shipped**: one shared `matchingRelativePaths` in `source-scan.ts`; the ten private
`listMatchingFiles` copies deleted; **156 lines removed**; errors now propagate, which is what all
twelve already did. Every allowlist verified **byte-identical to `HEAD`**, every `toContain` vacuity
control intact, and a planted offender still turns the gate red.

**The cost, which is the part worth remembering**: removing the shared idiom made ten gates
invisible to the meta-gates that read them. The classifiable-gate count fell **89 → 79** and
`allowlist-entries-still-apply` found 2 gates where it expects 3. Both caught it and both were
taught the new call — but a shared idiom is load-bearing for the machinery that reads it, and
changing one means updating that machinery in the same commit.

## Extension decided: `basename-line-references.test.ts` reads unbackticked citations — 2026-09-13

Feature 213 (FR-020, T1748), in the four-field shape
`specs/213-claims-nothing-verifies/contracts/sweep-outputs.md` §C4 requires of every decision this
cycle makes. **Recorded here rather than in the feature directory** because this file already holds
the tree's gate verdicts, and "zero retirements is a valid outcome" above is this decision's own
shape one level up: a decision about gate coverage, written in the affirmative whichever way it goes.

**Decision.** Extend the existing gate's extraction to **unbackticked** citations, as a **reporting**
check inside `tests/lint/basename-line-references.test.ts` — no new file, no second resolver. In code
files the extraction reads **comment ranges only**; in Markdown it keeps the existing non-fenced-prose
rule. The **semantic-staleness** check is declined. The **backtick convention** is declined as the
answer, and adopted only as the shape this feature's own repairs already use.

**Citations in commit messages are out of scope**, named here because the citation sweep hands one to
this decision by name: commit `90189b72`'s body attributes a removal to `e2bf9ad`, a ref that resolves
in no branch of this repository. The class is real and is this same defect one level up. It is
declined because a commit body is immutable once written, so a gate over it can only report history it
cannot repair, and because this gate's scan roots are the working tree — a pass over `git log` is a
different instrument with a different failure mode, not an extension of this one. Reopened if the tree
adopts a commit-message citation convention a hook can check at *write* time, which is the only point
where such a citation can still be fixed.

**Measurement.** `specs/213-claims-nothing-verifies/decisions.md` §M6 sized the class; §D-US4a
re-measured it after the three repairs: 140 citations in code comments, 46 unbackticked, 86 already
read by this gate, 40 unbackticked inside its scan roots. §M6's sample found the sharper fact —
**four of five semantically stale citations are green today**, because they are backticked, in scope,
and resolve to a file long enough to hold the line.

T1748 then measured this gate's own exposure, which is the number the decision actually rests on,
because §M6 counted code comments and this gate also scans `.md`:

| | Live tier | Dated records |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME:NN` shapes in scope | 260 | 5,233 |
| already backticked, so already read | 218 | 4,189 |
| **newly admitted by dropping the backtick** | **42** | **1,022** |
| of those, failing the gate's own rules | 12 | 33 dead bare names, 10 distinct |
| after restricting code files to comment ranges | **8** | unchanged (Markdown has no comments) |
| genuine defects among them | **7** | **5, across 3 basenames** |

**Reason.** Clarification Q4 fixed the rule before either sweep ran: *extend or register where the
uncovered set is small enough to enumerate by hand; decline any option requiring a heuristic over
prose.* Both halves decide a different part of this, and both were settled by measurement rather than
by argument.

*Small enough to enumerate by hand* is not asserted — the whole set is enumerated here. Specimens
are fenced throughout this section, for the reason the gate itself gives for skipping fences: quoted
material is not a citation the document makes, and a record that cannot exhibit a stale citation
without failing on it is unwritable.

The live tier's seven are six unbackticked comments and one backticked citation this gate cannot
parse. Not one is marginal drift — every one cites past the end of a file by a wide margin:

```text
cited                             file length   margin
workflow-controller.ts:1448           1007      +441
src/extension.ts:1157                  659      +498
src/extension.ts:1181                  659      +522
extension.ts:936    (bare)             659      +277
state-projector.ts:796-812             192      +620
PipelineCatalogEditor.svelte:310-325   153      +172   (backticked; see blind spots)
```

Every one is refused by the **reachability** rule this gate already has. Nothing new has to be
invented to catch them; they were invisible for want of a backtick. The record tier's five are three
deleted components — `AuditTail.svelte` and `QueueGlobalActions.svelte` (deleted by `16de985b`) and
`cmd-save-phases.ts` (by `e77a82bb`) — and both commits are **already cited in `KNOWN_ABSENT`** for
their siblings. Three names, in a ledger whose shape already fits them; that is what makes the set
hand-enumerable, which is all Q4's rule asks.

**No ledger entry is added for them, though**, and the reason is worth stating because the opposite
looks tidier. `KNOWN_ABSENT` waives the **blocking** record check. This extension does not block, so
there is nothing to waive: an entry would record a standing permission against a check that cannot
fail, and this tree has already had dead allowlists removed from three gates for being exactly that.
The report names all three and the census names their deleting commits, which is the information a
reader actually needs. Whoever later makes this pass block adds the entries in that change, where
the waiver means something.

*Decline any option requiring a heuristic over prose* is what kills the semantic-staleness check,
and the cost of declining is stated rather than hidden: §M6 shows semantic staleness is the larger
half of the real defect, and this decision leaves it uncovered. Asking whether line 812 still
*carries the claim* is a judgement about prose, and the strongest counter-argument on record — the
`asserted-counts.test.ts` docblock's, that a prose heuristic produces false positives and a gate with
false positives gets switched off — applies to it in full.

**That counter-argument was engaged against the extraction too, by experiment.** Dropping the
backtick over raw text produced **12** live-tier failures, and four of them were false:

```text
citing file                           the specimen                       what it actually is
history-sanitization.test.ts          a thrown stack trace               fixture input
command-trust-dispositions.test.ts    'synthetic.ts:2'                   fabricated path
audit-payload-v3.test.ts              /Users/someone/secret.ts:12        redaction input
workflow-pin-outcomes.test.ts         ci.yml:4, under a workflow dir        expected output
```

**All four sit inside string literals**, and none is a claim the file makes about the tree. The
fourth specimen is abbreviated above on purpose: written in full it names a CI directory this
repository does not have, and `current-control-claims.test.ts` reads that as a live claim — which is
this section's own subject arriving one level up, and a second reason a record must quote carefully.
Restricting extraction to comment ranges removed four of four and kept eight of eight — a lexical
distinction the language already makes, decided by the parser and not by a reader's judgement about
intent. So the registry's objection is answered by construction rather than overridden. Had the false
positives survived that rule, the honest answer would have been to decline this option too.

**Two blind spots found while measuring, neither about backticks**, both in the extraction pattern.
Each is a backticked, in-scope citation this gate has never read:

- **Line-wrapped citations are invisible.** `empty-situation-coverage.test.ts` hard-wraps a
  backticked citation mid-token, breaking after the hyphen in `webview-host-import-`. The gate reads
  line by line, so it sees a fragment carrying one backtick and skips it. The unbackticked pass
  reports it dead; the file exists and the citation is sound. This is the eighth live-tier hit and
  the one genuine false positive that survives the comment rule. **It is not fixed**, and the reason
  is the rule that shaped the decision above: reading it would mean joining physical lines before
  extracting, which turns a line-by-line reader into one that must decide where a wrapped citation
  ends — a judgement over prose, which Q4's rule declines. Its cost is bounded and known at one
  false positive, which is also why the extension ships as a reporting check rather than a blocking
  one.
- **Multi-range citations are invisible.** `PipelineToolbar.test.ts` cites two ranges of
  `PipelineCatalogEditor.svelte` as a single comma-joined token. The pattern requires the closing
  backtick immediately after `NN-MM`, so a comma-list is not extracted at all — and that file is
  **153 lines**, so both ranges are stale (tabulated above). Invisible for a reason that has nothing
  to do with backticks. The blocking pass still cannot see it; the reporting pass added by T1749
  does, incidentally, because without the closing backtick the first range matches on its own. So
  it is now reported and still not enforced, which is the right place for it: the citation is
  genuinely stale, and FR-022 confines this feature's repairs to three named sites.

**Revisit condition.** The semantic check is reopened when a **mechanical** discriminator exists for
it — a citation carrying a symbol name beside its location can be checked by string presence, which
is a lookup rather than a judgement. T1746 and T1747 repaired all four of this feature's citations
into exactly that form, so the tree is beginning to accumulate the evidence such a check would need.
Until then the answer is no, and the reason is the registry's, not indifference. The extraction
decision itself is settled.

The **two extraction blind spots** above are reopened on a different trigger, stated separately
because this condition does not cover them: when either stops being a single known instance — a
second hard-wrapped citation, or a second comma-joined multi-range. The argument for carrying each is
that one instance is cheaper to name than a pattern that must guess where a citation ends; a second
instance is the evidence that the shape recurs, and it retires that argument.

## Extension registered: `source-loc-budget.test.ts` reads the whole of `src/` — 2026-10-01

Feature 217 (`FR-R3-183`; FR-041, FR-047). The file gate gained an entry condition. Every `.ts`
file under `src/` of 1,000 lines or more must carry an entry in its table, a ceiling or a waiver. A
file that reaches the condition unlisted fails, named with its size, and the failure lists the three
states its author may choose. It is an extension of an existing gate, not a new file, so it adds no
row: the gate's row below records it. The decision, the distribution it was chosen from and what
would reopen it are in [size-gate-entry-condition.md](size-gate-entry-condition.md), and are not
repeated here.

**One overlap it created, and nothing retired.** The condition captured
`src/controller/phase-runner.ts`. Feature 057's `phase-runner-loc-budget.test.ts` already held that
file at its size, 1,403 lines by `wc -l`, which the filing that raised this missed. The waiver the
file now carries in the file gate holds the same size, so both rows below are marked
`partially redundant` for that one file. Of the two, feature 057's entry is the one that could go.
The file gate's waiver holds the same size and also has to come down when the file shrinks, and the
entry condition fails without it. Feature 057's entry was left in place, with a comment naming the
second bound. Feature 057's other three files are held by nothing else, so that gate stays whatever
is decided about this one entry.

| `task-transition-decision-census.test.ts` | every Task status writer routes through decideTaskTransition (FR-R3-153, T1637; population derived by FR-R3-161) | — | unique | no sibling gate, type, generated contract or compiler flag was found asserting this; see Method. **The population is derived, not listed.** Until FR-R3-161 this gate carried a hand-maintained five-name array and a header admitting "this file discovers nothing" — and it was wrong: it had never seen `src/state/queue-state-migrator.ts`'s surplus in-flight demotion, a genuine Task status writer consulting nothing, which is the exact defect the census exists to report. A list is silent about what nobody remembered to add to it. `tests/lint/task-status-writer-derivation.ts` now computes the population from source text in three stages — the file names `FeatureRequest`; the site is an object literal whose *first* top-level element is a spread and which also assigns `status` (colon form or shorthand), located by walking brace depth over source that has had comments, string bodies, template literals and regex bodies masked to spaces; the file also names `requests`. Every candidate must then be **enrolled** (its enclosing declaration calls `decideTaskTransition(` and reads `.eligible`) or **exempt** — named in an `EXEMPTIONS` table with a written reason *and* the number of sites the exemption covers, so a second write landing inside an already-excused function is a new decision rather than a covered one. Anything else is red: the gate fails **closed**, where the list it replaced merely fell silent. The population term is anchored on the Task record's NAME, never on a status *value* (every Task status spelling is also written onto a `WorkflowRun` in `run-driver.ts`, `controller/phase.ts`, `controller/retry-handler.ts` and `controller/task-deletion.ts`) and never on `as FeatureRequestStatus` (two enrolled writers write theirs uncast) — AGENTS.md rule 67, pinned by a regression test that fails if `commands/restart-canceled-task.ts` ever takes the cast. The derivation is deliberately over-inclusive: it cannot apply a semantic rule, so it selects three sites that write a workflow run rather than a Task and the table dismisses them by name, each reason stating which of the two kinds of exemption it is — a *writer the classifier cannot serve* (one, the migrator) or a *candidate that was never a writer* (the rest). A false positive costs one table line; a false negative is the failure the gate exists to prevent. Because the derivation is a pure function of a root directory it is called twice: over `src/` for the assertion, and over `tests/lint/fixtures/` for a negative control whose planted unenrolled writer can never reach the real gate, and whose deletion turns the control **red on an empty result** instead of passing silently. Driven red 2026-09-04 three ways: a leading-spread `status` write added to `queueIdForTask` (named in the failure, with its file, line and literal); the `cancel` exemption removed (named); the control fixture deleted (empty-result control) — all restored and re-run green, 13 tests. Derived population: **9 candidates, 5 enrolled and 4 exempt** — the steady state reached when FR-R3-161 deleted `QueueManager.cancel` on 2026-09-04, from the 10/5/5 the derivation first measured with it still present |
